Chapter 6: The Great Transformations—From the Routine of Fear to Storms of Change.
You ever notice how, at certain points in history, everything just... shifts? The rules everyone’s been living by suddenly stop making sense. That’s exactly what happened when the protests first broke out in Syria.
Fear wasn’t the only feeling in the air anymore. Suddenly, there was anxiety, confusion—maybe even a flicker of hope. Inside the security apparatus, you could feel the tension building. People were glued to the news, worrying about what might come next. The usual routines just weren’t enough to keep things steady; every day seemed to bring a new surprise.
Picture this: one morning, an employee walks into his office and finds his coworkers whispering about demonstrations spreading through the cities. No one really knows how they’re supposed to react. The orders are crystal clear—“No leniency with any suspicious movement.” But deep down, everyone’s torn. There’s the fear of losing control, sure, but also this urge to understand what’s really happening beyond those thick walls.
Out on the streets, people were changing, too. Silence wasn’t the norm anymore—voices started rising, demanding dignity and freedom. Imagine one of those workers, watching a group of young people writing slogans on a wall late at night. He doesn’t know what to do—report them right away, or try to get what’s driving them? In that moment, it hits him: the world he thought he knew is starting to crack.
Inside the organization, the pressure kept mounting. Orders got harsher, surveillance grew tighter. In one meeting, everyone was told to be extra alert—report anything unusual, even if it’s coming from people you trust the most. It felt like living on the edge, with tension hanging in the air every single day.
And as things escalated, some of the employees started feeling like outsiders in their own communities. One day, a worker tries to visit his family in the countryside. But he can sense the way people look at him—some are wary, others just avoid talking to him altogether. That’s when he realizes: the gap between him and the rest of society is wider than ever.
As each day passed, it became harder to believe that things could ever go back to the way they were. Many people on the inside started questioning what they were even doing, and what their future might hold in this rapidly changing world. One night, two colleagues sit together in a little café, reminiscing about their early days in the agency—the dreams that brought them there. There’s nostalgia in their voices, but also a clear sense of being lost.
So, as the events kept unfolding, it became obvious: these big transformations aren’t just about changing the face of society. They leave a deep mark on everyone—especially those who’ve spent their lives in the shadows. It’s not just fear anymore; new emotions have entered the picture, making everyone rethink their choices and what truly matters in their lives.
